plan: Store the constructor's data dictionary as a private deep copy so the workspace owns its state; return another deep copy from to_data() so callers can never mutate internals.

Implement one recursive pre-order generator over the item tree yielding (item, depth); drive total_word_count(), unresolved_markers(), and outline() from it so all read operations share the same deterministic list-order traversal.
Count note words by first replacing every [[?identifier]] marker token with a space, then counting \b\w+\b matches; add each reference's declared word_count directly.
Collect marker identifiers from note text via the marker regex and from reference 'unresolved' lists (normalizing full-token strings to bare identifiers), then return the sorted set.
Render the outline as the workspace title plus one line per item: two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at level 1) followed by '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and destination (literal 'workspace' means the root list), require a section/group destination, reject moving a container into itself or any descendant via a subtree scan, and range-check an explicit index against the destination length — all before any mutation, so a failed move raises ValueError with the tree untouched; only then pop from the old parent and append/insert into the destination.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at construction and to_data() boundaries
Single recursive pre-order tree walker shared by all read operations
Regex-based marker stripping/extraction ([[?identifier]] tokens) separated from \b\w+\b word counting
Kind-based dispatch: notes contribute parsed text words, references contribute declared word_count
Sorted-set aggregation for unique, lexicographically ordered marker identifiers
Validate-then-mutate move protocol guaranteeing atomicity of failed moves
Iterative subtree containment check to reject self/descendant destinations
